chunks: And from him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who is afflicted with a nosebleed while he is in salat (prayer). He said: “If he is able to reach water near him, to his right or left, in front of him, while he remains facing the qiblah, then let him wash it away from himself and then continue whatever remains of his salat (prayer). But if he is not able to reach water without turning his face away or speaking, then he has cut off his salat (prayer).”

key_terms.فَلْيَغْسِلْهُ: let him wash the blood away
key_terms.قَطَعَ صَلَاتَهُ: his prayer has been interrupted and nullified
key_terms.مَاءٍ: water used to wash away the blood
key_terms.مُسْتَقْبِلُ الْقِبْلَةِ: remaining oriented toward the qiblah during prayer
key_terms.يَتَكَلَّمَ: to speak, which invalidates continuity here

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if a nosebleed happens during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who experiences a nosebleed during salat (prayer). If he can wash the blood without breaking the prayer’s required orientation or speaking, he continues; otherwise, his salat (prayer) is invalidated and cut off.
